messages:
maria: FYI support escalated high p99/p95 for customers on eu-dedicated-2 — CS-4982. Seeing p99 ~2.7s and user timeouts around 09:12 UTC. They reported degraded UX on chat completions.

support-ade: I pulled the ticket logs. Errors look like upstream timeouts, interleaved with long cold-start logs. Customer trace attached here: https://redwood.internal/cs/CS-4982/trace (internal).

oncall-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool eu-dedicated-2 p99 latency spike > 2s (09:11:42 UTC). autoscale_events: scale_up_requested -> delayed_by_cooldown.

jamie: Can someone grab the pool provisioning logs and the autoscaler decision for that window? suspect scale-up lag + cloud GPU provisioning variance.

kevin: grabbing logs now. quick summary: pool had min_replicas=2, current_replicas=2, pending_scale=4, desired_replicas=6. Provision requests were sent at 09:11:10 but first GPU registered at 09:15:02. That's ~3.8m gap.

kevin: relevant snippet: ```
[09:11:10] autoscaler: request 4 gpus -> provider API accepted request id=pr-8372
[09:11:12] provider: ACK provisioning job j-9921
[09:12:30] autoscaler: cooldown check -> still within cooldown, no retry
[09:15:02] node join: gpu-node-eu-45
[09:15:10] serving: initialized kv-cache, warmed 0 prefixes
```

maria: That cooldown block looks suspicious — cooldown prevented retry and we never had warm standby. For dedicated pools we usually keep at least 1 warm replica for critical customers. Looks like config drift.

lina: I checked infra config, the pool config shows warm_pool_size=0 (was supposed to be 1). There's a PR that rolled back the warm pool last month (PR #4467).

sre-lead: Immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic for impacted customers to eu-dedicated-warm (warm pool) if capacity exists, 2) trigger manual warmup to spin VMs/GPU, 3) temporary overflow to hosted API with customer consent. Which can we do fastest?

jamie: We can do (2) and (3) now. I'll run warmup and then open overflow route.

kevin: running warmup command: ```bash
# manually request warm replicas
rctl pool warmup --pool eu-dedicated-2 --count 3 --reason "urgent-cs-4982"
```

deploy-bot: ACTION: warmup job created id=wu-331. Estimated provisioning time 3-5m.

support-ade: Support notified customer about temporary degraded performance and proposed fallback to hosted endpoints for critical requests. Customer agreed to try overflow for high-priority jobs.

maria: I patched the autoscale policy in place to reduce cooldown from 300s -> 60s for this pool and increased warm_pool_size to 1. Patch diff: ```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 12
  cooldown: 60  # lowered from 300
  warm_pool_size: 1
```

kevin: patch applied, restarting controller. controller logs show new policy active at 09:22:14. Also added retry path so provision failures will re-enqueue quicker.

oncall-bot: NOTE: overflow route enabled for customer AcmeCorp -> hosted fallback at 09:23:05 UTC.

maria: After warmup and overflow, p99 dropped to ~350ms for affected traffic that hit warm pool/hosted. For the rest p99 decayed to ~900ms as nodes joined and cache warmed.

kevin: root cause summary candidate: config drift removed warm_pool_size and long cooldown + provider provisioning variability. Consequence: traffic surge forced scale which couldn't provision quickly leading to high p95/p99.

sre-lead: Immediate follow-ups:
- create infra rollback of PR #4467 (reintroduce warm_pool_size) -> ACTION @kevin JIRA INFRA-972
- Add canary check that prevents warm_pool_size from being set to 0 for production pools -> ACTION @lina JIRA INFRA-973
- Add provider provisioning SLA guard (if provisioning >120s, trigger fallback earlier) -> ACTION @maria JIRA RUNTIME-881
- Run a tabletop on dedicated scale-up scenarios next Tues -> OWNER @sre-lead

jamie: I'll also add a short-term metric alert for (scale_up_requested && no_node_joined within 180s) to catch this earlier.

support-ade: Customer follow-up done — they want a short incident report and the timeline. I'll draft and share with CS by EOD.

maria: Estimating customer impact window: 09:11:10 - 09:23:05 UTC. Will include p95/p99 graphs and traces in the report.

kevin: One extra note: we saw KV-cache miss storms when new nodes came up; warming script didn't preseed prefixes. I'll add a change to warmup to run a seed job: ```bash
rctl pool seed-prefixes --pool eu-dedicated-2 --from recent_prompts --parallel 8
```

lina: tagging postmortem: severity=high, impacted_customers=["AcmeCorp"], root_causes=["config-drift", "provider-provisioning-variance"], mitigations_applied=["warmup", "overflow", "autoscale-policy-adjust"].

sre-lead: Good work triaging. Keep updates here. We'll close when JIRA tickets are created and customer report sent. :thumbsup:

maria: created INFRA-972, INFRA-973, RUNTIME-881, PM assigned to @lina. Sharing drafts shortly.

kevin: linking quick diffs + logs: https://redwood.internal/ops/CS-4982/logs and PRs https://redwood.internal/pr/4479.

support-ade: Customer confirmed degration acceptable during mitigation; monitoring for any regressions. closing escalation once PM sends final note. :white_check_mark:

maria: final note — we should consider a default policy enforcement so prod dedicated pools always have warm_pool_size >=1. I'll file a follow-up improvement after postmortem.

lina: noted. I'll include that in the postmortem action list.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT-TRACK: CS-4982 status -> mitigated (warmup + overflow) at 09:23:05 UTC.

maria: Thanks team — nice quick ops.
